PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 77 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 01/15/25 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for COPD management and evaluation of lower extremity edema.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit to assess his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and the ongoing issue of bilateral lower extremity edema. Since his last visit, he reports that his respiratory symptoms have remained stable, with no significant exacerbations. He continues to use his albuterol inhaler occasionally, about 1-2 times a day, particularly during cold weather, and his fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler remains effective in controlling his baseline symptoms.
The patient notes that while his cough has not returned, he still experiences intermittent mild wheezing, which he attributes to colder temperatures. His sleep patterns have improved further, with less nocturnal dyspnea, and he has been following recommendations for head elevation during sleep.
However, Mr. Fairfax expresses concern regarding persistent swelling in his legs, which he describes as 2+ pitting edema. He has been diligent in elevating his legs as advised, but the edema has not fully resolved. He denies any associated symptoms of pain, redness, or warmth in the extremities and has not experienced any shortness of breath or chest discomfort.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + stable energy levels, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - - cough, - sputum production, + mild wheezing, - dyspnea on exertion, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily 4. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain 5. Prednisone 5 mg daily (completed taper)
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 78, BP 126/74, RR 18, O2 sat 95% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 2+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.3, Hgb 13.6, Hct 40.1, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 138, K 4.1, Cl 100, CO2 28, BUN 15, Cr 0.9, Glucose 96 3. BNP: 420 (stable) 4. CXR: No significant changes from previous imaging, stable hyperinflation of lungs.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Continue current inhaler regimen. Educate the patient on the importance of adhering to medication schedules and recognizing early signs of exacerbation. Reassess in 2 months or sooner if symptoms worsen. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains well-controlled. Schedule follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: Initiate a trial of furosemide 20 mg daily for one week to assess response. Discussed lifestyle modifications including reduced sodium intake and continued leg elevation. 4. Follow up with pulmonary medicine for ongoing management.
Patient education reinforced regarding COPD self-management strategies and the importance of recognizing signs of fluid retention.
